newsitem.title: USA: Heart treatments produce same results after 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Heart treatments produce same results after 5 years.

text.p: Heart patients who undergo angioplasty treatments ultimately fare about the same in quality of life measures and relief of symptoms as those who undergo coronary bypass surgery, researchers said on Tuesday.

The less-invasive angioplasty -- a technique for opening narrowed or blocked arteries with a balloon-tip catheter -- also allowed patients to return to work more quickly, researchers from the Bypass Angioplasty Revascularization Investigation Group said in their study.

Coronary bypass patients, where healthy arteries are transplanted to replace diseased arteries feeding the heart, more frequently complained of limitations with housework and other social activities in the first follow-up evaluation four to 14 weeks after entering the study. About 36 percent of bypass patients had returned to work, compared to 55 percent of the angioplasty patients.

However, angioplasty patients were more likely to suffer from pain associated with inadequate blood flow during the first three years after initial treatment, and had to undergo repeated procedures, the study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association said.

"Otherwise, standard quality-of-life outcomes and behavioural risk factors were similar for the two treatment groups," study author George Sopko of the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute in Bethesda, Maryland, wrote.

"Over time, the treatment differences in angina and exercise-induced ischemia (inadequate blood flow to specific organs or tissues) diminished, due to a return of symptoms among (bypass) patients," he wrote.
